title: Hosted burst OOM throttler and KV cache metadata reconciler
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: A hosted customer experienced repeated GPU OOM spikes during short high-concurrency embedding workloads. Root cause analysis points to three correlated issues: (1) burst allocation patterns exposed fragmentation in the allocator, (2) stale/kick-started KV-cache metadata left dangling session handles which prevented efficient KV reuse, and (3) request concurrency control was insufficient for multi-tenant bursty workloads. This ticket implements a short-term throttler (per-tenant burst cap + token-rate limiter) and a KV-cache metadata reconciler that proactively heals stale tombstones and compacts metadata to reduce allocator pressure. The goal is a minimal-risk runtime patch that reduces immediate customer impact, followed by a larger cleanup (allocator compaction improvements + long-term KV index redesign).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a hosted inference pool with mixed tenants and default kvcache settings. 2) Run a synthetic workload that does 300 concurrent embedding sessions in 60s windows with varied sequence lengths (avg 1024 tokens). 3) Observe GPU memory climb above normal working set and sporadic OOMs after several bursts. 4) Inspect kvcache metadata: sessions with stale tombstone flags remain referenced by recent allocations and are not compacted under burst pressure.
investigation_summary: Timeline: customer reported errors 2026-02-26 02:14 UTC. On-call triaged; evicted offending sessions -> temporary relief. Heap/allocator traces and KV index dumps show high slab fragmentation and repeated small allocations pinned by leftover session handles. Memory profile showed >30% working set variance compared to baseline. We reproduced locally with the synthetic burst and confirmed two key failures: a race in session finalize path that left tombstones unreferenced, and allocator freelist starvation under short spikes.
mitigation_plan: 1) Emergency patch: add per-tenant burst throttler (soft cap 200 concurrent sessions, hard cap 400) with circuit-breaker fallback to a lightweight CPU-based embedding queue for excess load. 2) KV metadata reconciler: background sweep job that runs reconcilation every 30s on hosted nodes and coalesces tombstones older than 45s; this job is conservative and has an enable flag. 3) Allocator tuning: increase low-fragmentation threshold for burst windows and add transient slab reservation for incoming bursts. 4) Rollout: staged to hosted fleet (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with metrics gating (OOM count, tail latency, allocation churn).
tests_and_validation: Unit tests cover reconciler idempotency and tombstone boundary conditions. Integration test: synthetic-burst harness added to CI (runs in CI-special pipeline) to validate no regression. Load test: 6-hour soak with repeated bursts on canary nodes and telemetry capture. Metrics: OOMs per-hour, tail P99 latency, allocator churn rate, reconciler invocation count.
